title: Microsoft Dataverse: management MCP server for building and governing MCP servers
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and documented controls are supported, including the updated Microsoft 365 server-blocking guidance. The connector-policy path stops early, and the general premium-connector licensing statement needs an additional citation. Management-endpoint licensing and specific governance remain documented gaps, not promises of free use or inherited protection.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing for the management MCP server itself is not yet published, supporting model unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: MCPManagement licensing price Copilot Credits; management MCP licensing. Opened mcp-management and billing-licensing; searched Dataverse MCP costs. Published Dataverse data-tool and consuming-agent rules do not name entitlement for this management endpoint.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn labels the management MCP reference as preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature. ... Preview features have restricted functionality and aren't meant for production use.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The preview management reference does not publish a charge for the management server.
claims.quote: Searched: MCPManagement licensing price Copilot Credits; management MCP licensing. Opened the full mcp-management reference and billing-licensing; the management reference gives an endpoint and tool schemas, not a management-server price or billing meter.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio consuming agents may use Copilot Credits under their existing billing model.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.claim: Whether premium connectors need a licence depends on the consuming product and its licence.
claims.quote: If an instant flow has premium connectors, every user who runs the flow needs a Power Automate Premium license. In such cases, instead of licensing every user, you can license the flow with a Process license.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/faqs#how-do-power-automate-license-plans-work-for-flow-runs to sources for this general statement. The already-cited Copilot Studio billing page says its standalone subscription includes premium connectors.

claims.quote: Dataverse applies limits to how APIs are used. ... They affect only client applications that perform an extraordinary volume of API requests.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP availability is controlled in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server.
claims.quote: Select Manage > Environments. ... select Settings ... Product > Features. ... locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server

claims.claim: An API or command setting the Dataverse MCP environment availability switch is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse MCP disable API PowerShell Organization IsMCPEnabled; Dataverse MCP PowerShell enabled; Dataverse MCP Organization Web API enable. Opened data-platform-mcp-disable and CLI reference; found client allow automation, not an availability-switch operation.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Governance controls prose; Scope
claims.claim: The documented Dataverse client allow-list control covers the /api/mcp data entrypoint.
claims.quote: MCP allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint. MCP-named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and aren't restricted by this setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented that the Dataverse environment switch or client allow-list governs the management MCP endpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server disable; management MCP server access controls DLP roles audit disable. Opened data-platform-mcp-disable and mcp-management; one documents /api/mcp controls, the other the separate agent365.svc.cloud.microsoft management URL, without that relationship.

claims.claim: Allowed clients are configured at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Select Advanced Settings. ... Open the client record you want. ... On the MCP client record, set Is Enabled to Yes.

claims.claim: dataverse mcp allow <appId> allows the specified application as a Dataverse MCP client.
claims.quote: Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment. ... dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options]

claims.claim: The Dataverse CLI is preview.
claims.quote: Dataverse CLI reference (preview) ... This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The CLI client-allow command requires Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.
claims.quote: The authenticated user must have Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.

claims.claim: A registered MCP server can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization

claims.where: controls[2].note: Single tools; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Inside the selected MCP server, individual tools can be controlled through Tools > tool toggle.
claims.quote: Select the Tools tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an Enabled or Disabled toggle. ... Turn individual tools on or off as needed.

claims.claim: Individual-tool controls support only specific registered MCP server types.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: The documented individual-tool policy is enforced for supported experiences using the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway.
claims.quote: The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the policy at runtime for supported tools and experiences that use the gateway. Don't assume the policy applies across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 controls do not establish that blocking a server disables direct management-endpoint access outside governed pathways.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server ... blocks usage through governed Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) pathways. It doesn't automatically disable the underlying API or service endpoint outside that governed path unless separately controlled by service and API policy.

claims.claim: An API or command equivalent to the Microsoft 365 registry server-blocking control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 MCP server block tool enabled Microsoft Graph API registry; MCP server Graph block API Agent 365. Opened manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; the CLI reference explicitly removes develop-mcp block. No registry blocking API was found.

claims.claim: Connector data policy configuration starts at Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: select Security ... Data and privacy. ... select Data policy. ... select New Policy ... In the Prebuilt connectors section, select a Blockable connector ... Select Configure connectors and then Connector actions.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct policy wizard but stops early. Replace controls[3].ui.path and its rendered path with 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Configure connectors > Connector actions > Allow or Deny', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/connector-action-control.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy <policyDefinition> creates a connector data policy from a policy-definition object.
claims.quote: Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. ... New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy <Object> [-ApiVersion <String>]

claims.claim: The cited New-DlpPolicy operation belongs to Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module

claims.claim: Connector data policies can govern MCP tools consumed by Copilot Studio agents in scoped environments.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope. ... Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The cited classic data policy documentation does not establish governance of direct management-endpoint calls.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server access controls DLP roles audit disable; MCPManagement DLP policy. Opened mcp-management, admin-data-loss-prevention and advanced-connector-policies; documented reach is consuming agents and connector operations, not direct management-URL calls.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: UI and automation controls specific to management-endpoint availability and server/tool access are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server access controls DLP roles audit disable; management MCP server disable; MCPManagement DLP policy. Opened mcp-management, data-platform-mcp-disable, manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; found no direct-management control path or setting operation.

claims.claim: The management reference lists tools but does not describe how its roadmap DLP and server/tool governance model is configured or evaluated.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server access controls DLP roles audit disable; MCPManagement DLP policy. Read the full mcp-management reference: preview notice, endpoint, McpServers.Management.All scope and tool schemas, without DLP evaluation or server/tool access-control configuration.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies can block an entire listed MCP server.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not offer individual MCP-tool control.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed advanced connector policy coverage of direct management-endpoint calls.
claims.quote: Searched: MCPManagement DLP policy; management MCP server access controls DLP roles audit disable. Opened advanced-connector-policies and mcp-management; ACP describes listed MCP connector endpoints and connector runtime policy, not the direct management endpoint.
